([[Cary, North Carolina]]) | college = * [[Rice Owls men's basketball|Rice]] (2018–2020) * [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]] (2020–2021) | draft_year = 2021 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 17 | draft_team = [[Memphis Grizzlies]] | career_start = 2021 | years1 = {{nbay|2021|start}}–present | team1 = [[New Orleans Pelicans]] | years2 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021–2022]] | team2 = →[[Birmingham Squadron]] | highlights = }} '''Kenneth''' "'''Trey'''" '''Murphy III''' (born June 18, 2000) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Rice Owls men's basketball|Rice Owls]] and the [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia Cavaliers]]. With Virginia, he became the most recent (as of 2026) Men's NCAA basketball player to post a [[50–40–90 club#Men's NCAA|50–40–90 season]], with a 50–43–93 tally in the 2020–21 season. ==Early life== Murphy was born in [[Durham, North Carolina]], to his mother, Albeda, and father, Kenneth Murphy Jr.{{Cite web|url=https://virginiasports.com/player/trey-murphy-iii/|title=Trey Murphy III|date=June 19, 2020|website=Virginia Cavaliers Official Athletic Site}} He played high school basketball at [[Cary Academy]] in [[Cary, North Carolina]], where, as a senior, he averaged 24.7 points and 7.4 rebounds per game while shooting 49.4% from the floor.{{Cite web |title=NBA & ABA Players Who Attended High School in North Carolina |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/friv/high_schools.fcgi |access-date=August 7, 2022 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}} He also shot 43.6% from beyond the three-point line and 85.8% from the free-throw stripe. On October 4, 2017, Murphy committed to playing college basketball for [[Rice Owls men's basketball|Rice]].{{Cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Player/Trey-Murphy-46040054/TimelineEvents/|title=Trey Murphy Timeline Events|website=247sports.com}} Murphy had a notable growth spurt within high school standing 5'8 as a freshman and not reaching 6'4 until his senior year. He continued to grow in university, reaching his current height of 6'8 by the time of his draft. https://www.nba.com/watch/video/trey-murphy-iii-shares-stories-from-his-path-to-the-nba ==College career== ===Rice=== As a freshman, Murphy played in all 32 of Rice's games. He came off the bench 31 times and got to start one game, the first being against [[Charlotte 49ers men's basketball|Charlotte]] in March 2019. He averaged 8.4 points and 2.6 rebounds. He ranked fourth in [[Conference USA]] (C-USA) in three-point field goal percentage (42.1%) and 14th in 3-pointers made per game (2.0). He also set the school freshman record for three-point field goal percentage (42.1%). On January 26, 2019, Murphy scored a career-high of 24 points and five 3-pointers while going a career-best 6-of-6 from the free-throw line against UAB.{{Cite web|url=https://riceowls.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/trey-murphy-iii/5064|title=Trey Murphy III|website=Rice Owls}} As a sophomore, Murphy played in 29 of 32 games for Rice. He started in 23 of those games while coming off the bench in six. He led the Owls in scoring with 13.7 points and recorded 25 double-figure scoring games with two double-doubles. He also led the team with six 20-point games.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/trey-murphyiii-1.html|title=Trey Murphy III|website=Sports Reference}} ===Virginia=== On March 30, 2020, Murphy entered the transfer portal, and on April 14, 2020, he transferred to [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]].{{cite web|url=https://virginiasports.com/news/2020/04/16/mens-basketball-virginia-lands-transfer-trey-murphy-iii/|title=Virginia lands transfer Trey Murphy III|website=virginiasports.com|publisher=Virginia Sports|date=April 16, 2020|accessdate=April 12, 2021}} North Carolina native and friend Justin McKoy helped recruit him to Virginia.{{Cite web|url=https://wuvanews.com/meet-trey-murphy-iii/|title=Meet Trey Murphy III|website=WUVA News|date=April 16, 2020 }} Due to [[COVID-19]] affecting college basketball, Murphy did not have to sit out a year and was granted three years of immediate eligibility instead of two. Coming off the bench, Murphy scored 21 points while shooting 7-of-9 from the field in the Cavaliers' season opener in [[Bubbleville]]. He made his first start against [[William & Mary Tribe men's basketball|William & Mary]] in late December 2020 and started the remainder of the season.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/gamelog/_/id/4397688/trey-murphy-iii|title=Gamelog|website=ESPN}} At this time, NBA scouts saw him as a top 45 draft prospect.{{Cite web|url=https://augustafreepress.com/weekend-observations-juzang-trey-murphy-iii-vmi-heartbreaker/|title=Weekend Observations: Juzang, Trey Murphy III, VMI heartbreaker|website=Augusta Free Press}} As a junior, he averaged 11.3 points and 3.4 rebounds per game. After posting a highly efficient [[50–40–90 club|50–40–90]] season under [[Tony Bennett (basketball)|Tony Bennett]] at Virginia, Murphy declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility.{{cite web|url=https://www.streakingthelawn.com/2021/4/13/22381878/trey-murphy-iii-virginia-mens-basketball-acc-nba-draft|title=Trey Murphy III announces decision to enter NBA Draft, maintain eligibility|website=www.streakingthelawn.com|publisher=SB Nation|date=April 13, 2021|accessdate=April 13, 2021}} On June 21, 2021, Murphy announced that he signed with an [[sports agent|agent]], forgoing his remaining eligibility with Virginia and ending his collegiate career.{{cite web |last=Givony |first=Jonathan |title=Projected first-round pick Trey Murphy forgoes eligibility at Virginia, remains in NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31681693/projected-first-round-pick-trey-murphy-forgoes-eligibility-virginia-remains-nba-draft?platform=amp&__twitter_impression=true |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=June 21, 2021 |date=June 21, 2021}} ==Professional career== Murphy was selected with the 17th overall pick in the [[2021 NBA draft]] by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], but was traded to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-acquire-jonas-valanciunas-devonte-graham-three-team-trade-memphis-grizzlies-charlotte-hornets|title=Pelicans acquire Valančiūnas and Graham in three-team trade with Grizzlies and Hornets|work=NBA.com|date=August 7, 2021}}{{cite news |last1=Clark |first1=Christian |title=Pelicans take Trey Murphy with 17th pick, a Virginia forward with a smooth 3-point stroke |url=https://www.nola.com/sports/pelicans/article_8614f8f4-f0b2-11eb-b2f9-ebf48a7cb88b.html |access-date=July 30, 2021 |work=Nola.com |date=July 29, 2021}} On August 10, 2021, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Pelicans.{{cite web |title=Pelicans sign Trey Murphy III |url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-trey-murphy-iii |website=NBA.com |access-date=August 15, 2021 |date=August 10, 2021}} On October 20, Murphy made his NBA debut, recording six points and two assists in a 117–97 loss to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{Cite web |title=JOEL EMBIID, FURKAN KORKMAZ HELP 76ERS BEAT PELICANS 117-97 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100009 |access-date=February 6, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} The Pelicans qualified for the postseason for the first time since [[2018 NBA playoffs|2018]] and faced the [[Phoenix Suns]] during their first round series. Murphy made his playoff debut on April 17, recording six points, four rebounds and two assists in a 110–99 Game 1 loss.{{Cite web |title="CLASSIC CHRIS" STELLAR DOWN STRETCH, SUNS BEAT PELS 110-99 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042100141 |access-date=February 6, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} The Pelicans ended up losing the series in six games. During his rookie season, Murphy had multiple assignments to the Pelicans' [[NBA G League|G League]] affiliate, the [[Birmingham Squadron]].{{cite news |title=New Orleans Pelicans Assign Naji Marshall and Trey Murphy Iii to Birmingham Squadron |url=https://birmingham.gleague.nba.com/news/new-orleans-pelicans-assign-naji-marshall-and-trey-murphy-iii-to-birmingham-squadron/ |access-date=January 24, 2022 |work=Nola.com |date=January 22, 2022}} On February 5, 2023, Murphy scored a then season-high 30 points, alongside four rebounds and two assists, in a 136–104 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{Cite web |title=MURPHY SCORES SEASON-HIGH 30, PELICANS TOP KINGS 136-104 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200807 |access-date=February 6, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} In February 2023, Murphy was selected to participate in the [[Slam Dunk Contest]] at [[NBA All-Star Weekend|All Star Weekend]] in [[Salt Lake City|Salt Lake City, Utah]].{{Cite web |title=Trey Murphy grateful to receive NBA dunk contest, Rising Stars invites |url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/trey-murphy-grateful-to-receive-nba-dunk-contest-rising-stars-invites |access-date=February 16, 2023 |website=www.nba.com |date=February 15, 2023 |language=en}} He made it to the final round, but was defeated by [[Mac McClung]].{{cite web|url=https://www.thescore.com/nba/news/2578631|title=76ers' McClung takes home 2023 Slam Dunk crown|website=thescore.com|last=Soveta|first=Jonathan|date=February 19, 2023|access-date=March 12, 2023}} On March 12, Murphy put up a season-high and a then career-high 41 points in a 127–110 win over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/pelicans-news-trey-murphy-iii-epic-40-piece-will-make-giannis-antetokounmpo-devin-booker-proud|title=Trey Murphy III's epic 40-piece for Pelicans will make Giannis Antetokounmpo, Devin Booker proud|website=ClutchPoints|last=Guinhawa|first=Angelo|date=March 12, 2023|access-date=March 12, 2023}} On October 3, 2024, the Pelicans announced that Murphy would miss the start of the regular season due to a right hamstring strain that he suffered during an evening practice at their training camp.{{Cite web |last=MacMahon |first=Tim |date=October 3, 2024 |title=Pels' Murphy (hamstring) to miss start of season |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/41593253/pels-trey-murphy-hamstring-likely-start-regular-season |access-date=October 4, 2024 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} On October 21, Murphy signed a four-year, $112 million extension with the Pelicans.{{Cite web |last=Charania |first=Shams |date=October 21, 2024 |title=Sources: Trey Murphy, Pelicans agree to 4-year, $112M deal |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/41925450/sources-trey-murphy-pelicans-agree-4-year-112m-deal |access-date=October 21, 2024 |website=ESPN}} He played in 53 games (51 starts) for New Orleans during the [[2024–25 NBA season|season]], averaging career-highs in points (21.2), rebounds (5.1), and assists (3.5). On March 17, 2025, it was announced that Murphy would miss the remainder of the season after suffering a torn [[glenoid labrum|labrum]] and partial [[rotator cuff tear|tear of the rotator cuff]] in his right shoulder.{{Cite web |date=March 18, 2025 |title=Pelicans lose Murphy (shoulder) for rest of season |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/44298273/pelicans-trey-murphy-suffers-season-ending-torn-labrum-right-shoulder |access-date=2025-12-06 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press |language=en}} On January 4, 2026, Murphy made his 693rd career three-pointer and finished with 27 points, eight rebounds, five assists, one steal, and one block in a 125–106 loss to the [[Miami Heat]]. He also surpassed [[CJ McCollum]] to become the all-time leader in three-pointers made in Pelicans franchise history.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/new-orleans-pelicans/pelicans-news-trey-murphy-claims-all-time-franchise-record-heat-clash|title=Pelicans’ Trey Murphy claims all-time franchise record during Heat baskets|website=nba.com|last=Eichenhofer|first=Jim|date=January 4, 2026|access-date=January 5, 2026}} On January 6, Murphy put up a then career-high 42 points in a 111–103 loss to the [[Los Angeles
